title: CLAUDE.md
text: Allowed user-exported prefixes: - trk_* — Time-series tracks (signal following audio, e.g., F0, formants, energy) - lst_* — Summary statistics (scalars/vectors, e.g., jitter, voice quality measures) - ucnv_* — Unit conversions (Hz↔︎Bark/Mel/ERB/semitone, dB↔︎phon/sone) - read_* / write_* — /O SSFF, JSTF, audio Within trk_*, names follow trk_<metric>_<algorithm> metric non-obvious algorithm name. Examples: - trk_pitch_rapt, trk_pitch_swipe, trk_pitch_ac, trk_pitch_cc, … — pitch trackers - trk_pitchmark_estk, trk_pitchmark_reaper — pitch-mark detectors - trk_formant_burg, trk_formant_forest, trk_formant_snack, trk_formant_cgdzp, trk_formant_tvwlp — formant trackers - trk_rms, trk_acf, trk_zcr, trk_lpc, … — single-metric analyses (_ana suffix) - trk_dft_spectrum, trk_lps_spectrum, trk_css_spectrum — spectra (snake_case, never camelCase) Required trk_* functions: - Parameter: toFile (default FALSE), explicitExt, outputDirectory - Attributes: ext, tracks, outputType (“SSFF”), nativeFiletypes - Logic: Write SSFF toFile=TRUE, return AsspDataObj FALSE Standard parameters (applicable): - listOfFiles — Input path(s) - beginTime, endTime — Time windowing (seconds) - windowShift — Frame shift (ms) - minF, maxF — Pitch range - verbose — Progress messages

text: Layer 1: Core implementations - C/C++: ASSP (src/assp/), ESTk (src/ESTK/), SPTK (src/SPTK/), OpenSMILE (src/opensmile/), COVAREP (bundled C++) - pladdrr (Praat R) Praat-native algorithms Layer 2: Low-level Rcpp bindings (*_cpp functions) - Direct C++ bindings: rapt_cpp(), swipe_cpp(), reaper_cpp(), estk_pitchmark_cpp(), … - Require AsspDataObj input - Exposed R/RcppExports.R (auto-generated) - Always internal — never @export. Layer 3: High-level wrappers (user-facing) - trk_pitch_rapt(), trk_pitch_swipe(), trk_pitch_reaper(), trk_rms(), … etc. - Obtain audio via assp_load_audio_for_dsp() (uniform fallback contract) - Auto-parallelize 2+ files - Support toFile=TRUE/FALSE

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Audio-loading contract (every DSP wrapper): 1. Try framework’s native loader (libassp via processMediaFiles_LoadAndProcess(), pladdrr via av_load_for_pladdrr(), etc.) 2. failure / unsupported format, fall back read_audio() (libassp--av) 3. framework can’t consume AsspDataObj, dump temp WAV via avaudio_to_tempfile() pass path assp_load_audio_for_dsp(file, begin, end, samples, framework) (R/audio_loader.R) wraps contract — call new wrappers. Public reader: read_audio(fname, begin = 0, end = 0, samples = FALSE) — single user-facing audio loader. Mirrors wrassp::read.AsspDataObj. Sample-accurate windowing variable-rate containers via av::av_media_info(). Key internal helpers (@keywords internal): - R/av_helpers.R — av_to_asspDataObj(), processMediaFiles_LoadAndProcess() - R/pladdrr_helpers.R — av_load_for_pladdrr() - R/s7_avaudio.R — read_avaudio(), as_avaudio(), avaudio_to_tempfile() (S7 internal dispatch) - R/prep_recode.R — prep_recode() (-memory transcoding) S7 AVAudio class (internal): used memory-dispatch s7_methods.R. class constructor helpers exported; users obtain audio data via read_audio() returning AsspDataObj. Lossy-input warning (design goal): applying DSP routine lossy-encoded signal presents warning. Two paths cover : - Batch libassp wrappers — processMediaFiles_LoadAndProcess() (R/av_helpers.R) warns non-lossless input (gated verbose). - Single-file / newer wrappers — assp_load_audio_for_dsp() calls .warn_if_lossy_input() (R/audio_loader.R), checks extension knownLossless() (R/assp_types.R) emits cli::cli_warn(...) per file per session (via .frequency/.frequency_id). New wrappers route audio assp_load_audio_for_dsp() get free. warning lives DSP-loading helper, read_audio() — raw /O may called lossy audio intentionally. Lossless set: wav, flac, aiff, wv, ape, tta, caf, au, w64, dsf, dff, kay, nist, nsp. Anything else (mp3, aac, ogg/vorbis, opus, wma, m4a, …) treated lossy. Error/warning reporting: use cli::cli_warn/cli::cli_abort formatters R/error_helpers.R (format_processing_error, format_processing_warning, format_validation_error, safe_error_message) — bare warning()/stop() — user-facing messages (including data-loss notices) consistent (design goal: robust reporting).

text: Selected pladdrr-based voice analysis functions (trk_praatsauce, lst_pharyngeal, lst_voice_tremor) now include bug fixes plabench (companion project R re-implementations Praat algorithms). Fixes integrated: praatsauce: Unvoiced F0 frames now 0 (NaN); spectral guard adds != 0 check alongside !.nan() pharyngeal: Window sizes pitch-independent (onset 40ms fixed, mid ±20ms fixed); onset spectral window anchored intensity max (interval start); UNDEFINED sentinel → NaN tremor: Pitch intensity extraction moved FCoM gate (ensures FCoM computed even ftrf=0) intensity: Energy-domain mean computed explicitly (10*log10(mean(10^(frames/10)))) Praat-exact behavior changes align superassp’s pladdrr backends fixed behavior plabench. API changes; frame-level output may differ (unvoiced f0 now 0, NaN praatsauce — user code checking .nan(f0) may need updating f0 == 0).

title: CLAUDE.md
text: RcppXsimd dependency (DESCRIPTION LinkingTo; -DRCPPXSIMD_AVAILABLE src/Makevars). Vectorize hot numeric loops (dot products, energy sums, FIR/convolution, autocorrelation) using guarded pattern — never unconditionally, always scalar fallback: Reusable primitives: src/simd_utils.hpp — sasp::simd_dot, sasp::simd_energy, sasp::simd_fir (header-, double precision). Prefer hand-rolling. Precision rule: use xsimd::batch<double> unless scalar reference already float (e.g. src/yin_wrapper.cpp). Double keeps SIMD output equal scalar within testthat’s default expect_equal tolerance. architecture flags: add -march=native / -mavx* src/Makevars — non-reproducible CRAN-hostile. xsimd uses compiler’s baseline ISA (SSE2/NEON), portable already existing SIMD kernels build. Canonical examples: src/yin_wrapper.cpp, src/srh_variant.cpp (autocorrelation/energy/FIR). Faithfulness guarded tests/testthat/test-simd.R (SIMD vs base-R reference).
code: #ifdef RCPPXSIMD_AVAILABLE   using batch_type = xsimd::simd_type<double>;   // double: faithful to scalar (goal #1)   // ... xsimd batches + xsimd::hadd reduction + scalar tail ... #else   // plain scalar loop #endif

title: SSFF and JSTF: reading, writing, and round-tripping
text: Write track disk, read back read_ssff(): write_ssff() inverse operation, writing AsspDataObj built modified R: read_track()/write_track() format-agnostic dispatchers: pass trk_* output path detect SSFF vs. JSTF file’s metadata rather file extension.
code: wav <- system.file("samples", "sustained", "a1.wav", package = "superassp") out_dir <- tempdir()  trk_pitch_rapt(wav, toFile = TRUE, outputDirectory = out_dir, explicitExt = "f0") #> Applying `trk_pitch_rapt()` to 1 recording #> Successfully processed 1 of 1 file  f0_path <- file.path(out_dir, paste0(tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(wav)), ".f0")) f0_obj <- read_ssff(f0_path) track_names(f0_obj) #> [1] "f0" sample_rate(f0_obj) #> [1] 100 f0_obj[["f0"]][1:5, ] <- 0  # zero out the first 5 frames out_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".f0") write_ssff(f0_obj, out_path) read_ssff(out_path)[["f0"]][1:5, ] #> [1] 0 0 0 0 0

title: Voice quality and creak
text: Two creak detectors available output schema (creak_pp: posterior probability; creak_bin: binary decision), interchangeable downstream code: trk_creak_vat() — bit-faithful Rcpp port Kane-Drugman + Ishi ANN pipeline MATLAB Voice Analysis Toolkit. title: ISO 226:2023 Phon (Loudness Level) Conversions — iso226_phon
text: Functions converting sound pressure level (dB) loudness level (phon) according ISO 226:2023 "Acoustics - Normal equal-loudness-level contours".

title: ISO 226:2023 Phon (Loudness Level) Conversions — iso226_phon
text: phon scale represents loudness level - perceived loudness sound compared 1000 Hz reference tone. Unlike psychoacoustic scales (Bark, ERB, Mel), phon bivariate measure requiring frequency sound pressure level. Key concept: sound 40 phon sounds loud 1000 Hz tone 40 dB SPL, different frequencies require different SPLs achieve loudness. Valid ranges (per ISO 226:2023): Frequency: 20 Hz 12,500 Hz Loudness level: 20 phon 90 phon (20-4000 Hz), 20-80 phon (5000-12500 Hz) 20 phon: Informative (near hearing threshold) 90/80 phon: Limited experimental data Implementation notes: Based ISO 226:2023 Formulas (1) (2) Parameters ISO 226:2023 Table 1 Interpolation used frequencies standard 1/3-octave values Free-field listening conditions (frontal incidence, binaural)

title: ISO 226:2023 Phon (Loudness Level) Conversions — iso226_phon
ISO 532 Sone (Loudness) Conversions — iso532-sone
text: Functions converting phon (loudness level) sone (loudness) according ISO 532 standards. Sone linear unit perceived loudness, 1 sone = 40 phons definition.

title: ISO 532 Sone (Loudness) Conversions — iso532-sone
text: Two ISO 532 methods supported: ISO 532-1 (Zwicker method): Uses piecewise mathematical formulas ISO 532-2 (Moore-Glasberg method): Uses lookup table interpolation

title: ISO 532 Sone (Loudness) Conversions — iso532-sone
text: Zwicker method uses different formulas depending loudness level: sone < 1 (phon < 40): $$L_N = 40 \times S^{0.35}$$ sone >= 1 (phon >= 40): $$L_N = 40 + 10 \times \log_2(S)$$ Inverse formulas: phon < 40: $$S = (L_N / 40)^{1/0.35} = (L_N / 40)^{2.857}$$ phon >= 40: $$S = 2^{(L_N - 40) / 10}$$

title: ISO 532 Sone (Loudness) Conversions — iso532-sone
text: Uses lookup table 23 reference points 0.001 sone (0 phon) 337.6 sone (120 phon), log-linear interpolation.

title: ISO 532 Sone (Loudness) Conversions — iso532-sone
text: Reference: 1 sone = 40 phons = 40 dB SPL 1 kHz Doubling: 10 phon increase ~= doubles loudness sones Linear perception: Sones represent linear loudness (2 sones = 2x louder) Stevens' power law: Loudness proportional intensity^0.3

title: SEDREAMS Glottal Closure Instant Detection — lst_covarep_gci_sedreams
text: SEDREAMS Algorithm (Ney Kneser 2002) : Compute LPC residual (25ms frames, 5ms shift, order ≈ fs/1000 + 2) Bandpass filter signal around estimated F0 (mean-based signal) Find maxima/minima pairs mean-based signal Locate GCI positions LP residual peaks within windows Typical output: Voiced speech: 100-200 GCIs per second (F0-dependent) Unvoiced/silence: 0 GCIs (glottal closures) Use cases: Foundation GCI-based voice quality (NAQ, QOQ, H1H2 via trk_covarep_vq_gci) Voice pathology assessment (irregular GCI spacing = vocal pathology) Glottal source analysis (GCI-anchored inverse filtering) Speech analysis (pitch period estimation, voicing detection) Downstream workflow: lst_covarep_gci_sedreams() — detect GCIs trk_covarep_vq_gci() — compute voice quality per GCI lst_covarep_vq() — summarize scalars

title: SEDREAMS Glottal Closure Instant Detection — lst_covarep_gci_sedreams
text: Ney H, Kneser R (2002). “Speech recognition using continuous-space embeddings.” IEEE Signal Processing Magazine, 19(1), 33–42. Signal processing foundations GCI detection SEDREAMS algorithm.

title: Pharyngeal Voice Quality Analysis — lst_pharyngeal
text: Algorithm (based scriptPharyFullV4.praat): Two-pass adaptive pitch detection (speaker-specific F0 range) Find intensity maxima onset/midpoint Extract formants F1/F2/F3 bandwidths Extract 40ms Kaiser2 window onset Create spectrum pre-emphasis Find H1, H2 harmonics near F0, 2×F0 Find A1, A2, A3 formant peaks near F1/F2/F3 Apply Iseli & Alwan (2004) normalization Calculate differences (raw normalized) duration > 120ms, repeat midpoint Key Measures: H1-H2: Open quotient indicator (higher = breathier) H1-A1: Voice quality indicator (higher = breathier) H1-A2: Spectral tilt measure H1-A3: High-frequency energy indicator Normalized (*_norm): Corrected formant influence (Iseli & Alwan 2004) Typical Values: H1-H2: -10 +10 dB H1-A1: -5 +5 dB H1-A3: Often negative (A3 > H1) Performance: ~24ms per vowel (15.7x faster v4.8.14)

title: Signal polarity detection (RESKEW algorithm) — lst_polarity
text: Algorithm (RESKEW, Drugman et al.): High-pass filter signal 490 Hz cutoff (removes low-frequency noise/drift) Compute LP residual order = fs/1000 + 2 samples, 25ms frames, 5ms shift Compare residual skewness: unfiltered vs. high-pass filtered Polarity = sign(skew_filtered - skew_unfiltered) Interpretation: +1: Normal polarity (positive peaks vocal pulses) -1: Inverted polarity (flip signal processing) Note: skewness values close, result may unstable. Recommend confidence threshold: |result| > 0.1 reliable polarity detection.

title: Vowel space analysis (F1×F2 area ratio) — lst_vowel_space
text: Algorithm: Filter formant data gender-specific frequency ranges identify candidate vowels Run k-means clustering using reference vowel centroids initialization Match estimated centroids reference vowels using Mahalanobis distance Compute convex hull matched vowel points (actual vowel space) Compute convex hull reference vowels Ratio = actual area / reference area Interpretation: Ratio = 1.0: perfect agreement reference vowel space Ratio < 1.0: speaker reduced vowel space (dysarthria, age, etc.) Ratio > 1.0: speaker expanded vowel space (hyperarticulation, singing) NaN/error: insufficient vowel tokens (<1000 frames) valid range Reference vowel sets: Triangle: //, //, /u/ (corner vowels) Polygon: //, /ε/, //, /u/ (4-vowel system) Minimum frame requirement: 1000 frames must within gender-specific frequency bounds, function returns 0 ratio (insufficient data).

title: Extract harmonic model phase distortion features (HMPD): AE, PDM, PDD — trk_hmpd
text: toFile = FALSE: AsspDataObj tracks: ae FLOAT, Mel-frequency-warped cepstral amplitude envelope, n_frames × 25 (coefficients 0–24). Dimensionless (log-amplitude units). pdm FLOAT, phase deviation mean log-harmonic scale, n_frames × 25. Units: radians. pdd FLOAT, phase deviation deviation (aperiodicity), n_frames × 13. Larger values indicate noise-like phase scatter. Frame rate: 100 Hz (10 ms grid, resampled variable-rate sinusoidal analysis). toFile = TRUE: character vector output file paths, returned invisibly.

title: Extract harmonic model phase distortion features (HMPD): AE, PDM, PDD — trk_hmpd
text: HMPD captures spectral shape (AE) aperiodicity-related phase scatter (PDM, PDD). Phase deviations computed relative deterministic sinusoidal model harmonic; mean standard deviation across harmonics give PDM PDD. f0s NULL function falls back constant 100 Hz F0 emits warning. AE computed Mel-cepstrum (method 2 COVAREP). PDM uses log-harmonic scale 8 harmonics linear region (Bezier interpolation ). PDD derived circular phase variance.

title: Extract harmonic model phase distortion features (HMPD): AE, PDM, PDD — trk_hmpd
text: Degottex G, Kane J, Drugman T, Raitio T, Scherer S (2014). “COVAREP: collaborative voice analysis repository speech technologies.” Proceedings 2014 IEEE International Conference Acoustics, Speech Signal Processing (ICASSP), 960–964. doi:10.1109/ICASSP.2014.6853739 . Open-source toolkit voice analysis including HMPD, GCI detection, formants, pitch, voice quality measures, https://github.com/covarep/covarep.

title: Track spectral tilt using D'Alessandro PeakSlope (Morlet wavelet) — trk_peakslope
text: Spectral tilt estimated fitting linear slope across peak magnitudes seven Morlet wavelet scales. Lower (negative) values indicate steeper spectral slope, associated creakier phonation; higher values indicate breathier modal phonation. Seven D'Alessandro Morlet wavelets octave-spaced scales (2^0 2^6) convolved signal. maximum magnitude 40 ms frame taken per scale, log10-transformed, linear regression slope computed across seven scale-magnitude pairs.

Must match forward conversion method. title: Convert Bark Scale to Frequency — ucnv_bark_to_hz
text: inverse formulas derived analytically possible: Traunmüller (1990) (default): $$f = \frac{1960 \cdot (Bark + 0.53)}{26.81 - (Bark + 0.53)}$$ Note: Bark < 2, input adjusted account low-frequency correction forward transform. Wang, Sekey & Gersho (1992): $$f = 600 \cdot \sinh\left(\frac{Bark}{6}\right)$$ Zwicker: Uses numerical root-finding (uniroot) since inverse analytically solvable.

title: Convert Frequency to Bark Scale — ucnv_hz_to_bark
text: Three different approximation formulas available: Traunmüller (1990) (default): $$Bark = \frac{26.81 \cdot f}{1960 + f} - 0.53$$ Valid range: approximately 20-15500 Hz. Values 2 Bark adjusted \(Bark_{adjusted} = Bark + 0.15 \cdot (2 - Bark)\). Zwicker: $$Bark = 13 \cdot \arctan(0.00076 \cdot f) + 3.5 \cdot \arctan\left(\frac{f}{7500}\right)^2$$ Wang, Sekey & Gersho (1992): $$Bark = 6 \cdot \sinh^{-1}\left(\frac{f}{600}\right)$$

title: Convert Loudness Level (Phon) and Frequency to Sound Pressure Level — ucnv_phon_and_hz_to_db
text: function implements Formula (1) ISO 226:2023 Section 4.1. Loudness level (phon) represents perceived loudness sound. function calculates sound pressure level required given frequency achieve specified loudness level. Valid ranges: Frequency: 20-12500 Hz (1/3-octave standard frequencies) Phon: 20-90 phon (20-4000 Hz), 20-80 phon (5000-12500 Hz) 20 phon: Informative (near hearing threshold) limits: Limited experimental data Interpolation: Frequencies standard 1/3-octave values interpolated log-frequency scale. Vectorization: phon freq_hz can vectors. vectors, must length, one must length 1 (recycled).

title: superassp 0.8.2
text: DeepFormants Algorithm (Dissen & Keshet, 2017): - LPC analysis optimized Levinson-Durbin recursion (Numba JIT) - Deep neural network trained labeled formant data - Two modes: Tracking (RNN) Estimation (feedforward) - Pre-trained models included package Python Dependencies: - torch - PyTorch deep learning framework - numpy - Numerical computing - scipy - LPC analysis signal processing - pandas - Data manipulation - numba - JIT compilation (2-3x speedup) Pre-trained Models: - Estimation model: estimation_model.dat (16 MB) - Tracking model: LPC_NN.pt (3.9 MB) - Trained diverse speech datasets Performance vs Traditional Methods: - DeepFormants: Higher accuracy, slower (~5s 2.3s audio) - Forest (ASSP): Lower accuracy, faster (~150ms 3s audio) - Trade-: Accuracy vs. Speed - Best : Research, difficult speech, high-accuracy needs
